text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `pd-service:lb-targets-unhealthy-eu` - observed spike in 5xx from EU edge (x509/TLS handshake and 502 from ALB). Auto-page to oncall.
pagerduty: Notification: Alert `LB targets unhealthy (eu-prod)` - triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:01Z
matt.h: acked. I'm taking initial triage. Anyone oncall in EU region?
sara.k: @matt.h I just woke up, can help with failover if needed. grabbing console.
jon: seeing the same in synthetic checks — curl to api.eu.redwood.prod returns TLS handshake errors intermittently.
olivia: Customer support: getting several chats reporting 502s and logins failing for EU users. Roughly ~8% of requests in the last 5m.
infra-sre: ALB metrics show target group health dropping to 62% in eu-west-1. Backend NLB still reports healthy.
oncall-manual: handoff: i'm oncall for infra today. joining.
matt.h: quick scope: are these TLS cipher mismatches or backend misconfig? I see two patterns in logs:
matt.h: ```
# curl output from synthetic
$ curl -v https://api.eu.redwood.prod/health
* TCP connection to api.eu.redwood.prod port 443 failed: Connection refused
* SSL connection using TLSv1.2 / ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* SSL: certificate subject: CN=api.eu.redwood.prod
* curl: (35) SSL read: errno=0
``` 
sara.k: also pulled tcpdump at the edge LB - there are TLS 'alert' records around the same time. snippet:
sara.k: ```
12:01:23.123456 IP edge-lb -> backend: TLSv1.2 Alert (Level: Fatal, Description: Handshake Failure)
12:01:23.123789 IP backend -> edge-lb: RST
``` 
jon: health check logs from target show `HTTP 503` then `504` then `TLS handshake failure` in the same second for multiple hosts.
olivia: customers impacted: login, streaming completions, and evaluation jobs for EU tenants. estimating 6-12% request failure rate depending on route.
infra-sre: checking recent deploys — no infra deploys in the last 12h. App deploys three hours ago but only to canary and not EU prod.
matt.h: ok, next steps: 1) move traffic away from failing target group via weight shift; 2) if persistent, failover region/edge; 3) update PD and support with ETA.
oncall-manual: executing weight shift: increasing weight to eu-secondary-lb by 30% to relieve primary targets. running command now.
oncall-manual: ```
# shift weights
aws route53 change-weighted-record-set --id ZABC123 --set-weight 0.3
``` 
pagerduty: Note: automated escalation in 5m if not acknowledged by next tier.
sara.k: i see success in metrics — requests to primary target group down 40% in last 60s; error rate for primary dropped to 3%.
jon: pref. run a graceful drain on the affected target group to allow KV cache to be preserved: set deregistration delay to 300s and mark unhealthy.
infra-sre: marked failing instances `tg-eu-01, tg-eu-04` as draining. starting SSH to check process state.
olivia: filed initial CS update: "We are aware of increased 502/handshake errors in EU region, mitigation underway (traffic shifted). We'll follow up in 30min." sent to priority customers.
matt.h: checking ALB logs, seeing `ELB 204.10.11.5:443 -> 10.0.12.45:443 TLS alert handshake_failure` repeated. Opening a support ticket with cloud provider in parallel.
emma: one quick thought — we've rolled a new OpenSSL patch on some fleets in the past week. Could be cipher negotiation mismatch across edge/host. Has anyone validated cipher lists post-deploy?
jon: good call. comparing cipher lists now.
jon: found a host with `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` vs some with `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` (TLS1.3) — mismatch shouldn't break TLS1.2 fallbacks, but config drift possible.
infra-sre: SSHed into tg-eu-04: process `proxy-worker` had repeated TLS handshake exceptions in system logs. stack trace attached to thread (copied below):
infra-sre: ```
2026-03-15T09:10:52Z proxy-worker[pid=4321]: ERR TLS handshake failed: unexpected eof
2026-03-15T09:10:52Z proxy-worker[pid=4321]: ERR SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number
``` 
matt.h: mitigation plan: keep weight on secondary, drain the failing hosts, rotate certs? Let's avoid cert rotation unless confirmed. Prefer to restart proxy-worker on failing hosts and monitor.
oncall-manual: restarting proxy-worker on tg-eu-01 and tg-eu-04 now.
oncall-manual: restart done. health checks show tg-eu-01 recovered, tg-eu-04 still flapping.
jon: tg-eu-04 has network path issues to edge LB — investigating node-level network stack. running `ss -tnp` and `iptables -L`.
olivia: support queue: 14 open tickets flagged P1/P2, pushing an update to customers: next update in 15m with mitigation status.
infra-sre: found stray iptables rule blocking outbound ephemeral ports on tg-eu-04, unclear why. removing the rule.
infra-sre: iptables rule removed, tcpdump shows successful handshake now.
sara.k: metrics: error rate back under 1% for majority of routes. monitoring for a few minutes before we shift weight back.
matt.h: important: we need a followup action item — audit recent config automation runs that touched iptables and OpenSSL changes. Add to postmortem.
oncall-manual: marking alert as acknowledged and closing PD incident after stabilization.
pagerduty: Alert acknowledged by matt.h at 2026-03-15T09:18:05Z. No further escalations.
olivia: sending final customer update now: "Issue mitigated; cause under investigation; postmortem to follow."
emma: would like an RCA: suspect config drift from a partial Ansible run combined with a kernel update that changed crypto stack ordering.
matt.h: agree — capture timeline and runbook items. i'll open the incident ticket and assign owners: infra-sre for config audit, eng-runtime for proxy-worker hardening, product/comms for customer notes.
jon: adding logs to incident ticket and saving tcpdumps to s3: s3://redwood-incidents/5167894321/
matt.h: thanks everyone. leaving it to infra-sre and eng-runtime for deeper triage. closing thread here but keep oncall in loop for 1h monitoring. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-03-15-0423. Postmortem due in 72h.
